You are beefing up **system health/status** for the Nxeon platform at /opt/nxeon (Next.js App Router + Prisma + Postgres + serial job worker). Two surfaces: the PUBLIC marketing status page and a DEEPER admin health dashboard. Both must read ONE shared health layer so they never disagree.

## Current state (verified by a mapping pass — trust these file:line facts)
- Public status: `app/status/page.tsx` shows 4 components (web/proxmox/worker/db) via `getHealth()` in `lib/monitoring.ts`. Data is LIVE probes only, NO history: `web` is hardcoded "operational"; `db` = `SELECT 1`; `worker` = inferred from the Job table (QUEUED>2min ⇒ down, RUNNING>15min ⇒ degraded); `proxmox` = live GET /nodes/{node}/status per enabled Node row. `overallStatus()` rolls up worst-of. `app/api/health/route.ts` caches getHealth 15s and SANITIZES detail for the public (replaces raw error text with fixed PUBLIC_DETAIL strings — PRESERVE this; never leak internals publicly). `lib/status-copy.ts` is type-only/client-safe, shared with `components/marketing/MarketingFooter.tsx`. The status page copy claims "refresh ~15s" but there is NO client auto-refresh today.
- Admin health: `app/admin/monitoring/page.tsx` (+ client `components/admin/NodeMetrics.tsx`), gated `await requireArea("fleet")`. Shows worker status, stuck jobs, backup age summary, per-node RAM/CPU/disk MeterBars, a live VM table (listVms joined to Server by vmid). It already imports the SAME `lib/monitoring.ts`.

## Schema is ALREADY in the DB + client generated — do NOT edit prisma/schema.prisma
New models to USE: `HealthSample` (component,status,latencyMs?,detail?,ts) — periodic snapshot; `StatusIncident` (component?,severity[degraded|down|maintenance],title,body,startedAt,resolvedAt?,auto,createdAt,updatedAt). Also `ErrorLog` exists (owned by another stream — do not touch its writers).

## What to build
**Shared data layer (extend `lib/monitoring.ts`):**
- A `sampleHealth()` function that runs the existing component probes and WRITES one `HealthSample` row per component per call. Also auto-manages `StatusIncident`: when a component is down/degraded for N consecutive samples, auto-open an incident (auto=true) if none open; when it recovers, stamp `resolvedAt`. Keep it idempotent and cheap.
- Reader helpers: uptime % per component over a window (from HealthSample), a recent health timeline, open + recent-resolved incidents.
- This runs on the worker monitor cadence. You OWN `worker/monitor.ts` — add the sampleHealth call there OR export it for the loop. I will add the call site in `worker/index.ts` (next to `sampleServerDisks()` at ~line 1301) — tell me the EXACT line in your report.

**Public status page (`app/status/page.tsx`):** add real depth — per-component uptime % (e.g. 90-day), a visual health timeline/history strip, an incident history section (open + past incidents with timeline), and a small CLIENT auto-refresh component so the page actually refreshes (respect the "~15s" copy) WITHOUT leaking internals. Keep the sanitization: public surface shows friendly names + incident titles/bodies you deem public, never raw upstream error `detail`.

**Admin health dashboard (`app/admin/monitoring/page.tsx`):** go deeper than public — live queue depth + job failure rate (last 24h from Job table), node resource pressure with the existing MeterBars, disk/backup freshness (backupSummary already exists), per-subsystem drill-down, uptime numbers, and an incident management panel (post/resolve a manual `StatusIncident`) via a new ADMIN-gated `lib/actions-status.ts`. Keep `requireArea("fleet")`.

## Files you OWN
- `lib/monitoring.ts` (extend — do not break existing exports used by the public page, admin page, and MarketingFooter)
- `lib/status-copy.ts` (extend if needed; keep it client-safe/type-only imports)
- `app/status/page.tsx`, `app/api/health/route.ts`
- `components/status/**` (new client components: timeline, auto-refresh, incident list)
- `app/admin/monitoring/page.tsx`, `components/admin/NodeMetrics.tsx`, and new `components/admin/health/**`
- `worker/monitor.ts` (add sampleHealth)
- `lib/actions-status.ts` (new; ADMIN-gated incident post/resolve)
- `test/health-*.test.ts`

## Files you must NOT touch (report instructions instead)
- `prisma/schema.prisma` (frozen)
- `worker/index.ts` — tell me the exact call line to add in the monitor loop
- `lib/log.ts`, `app/admin/logs/**`, `lib/admin-groups.ts`, `lib/rbac.ts` (other streams / central)

## Platform rules (non-negotiable)
- `"use server"` = every export is a public endpoint; `lib/actions-status.ts` incident-management exports must `requireArea("fleet")` (admin) INSIDE each function. Public health readers used by app/status must NOT leak internal error text.
- Honesty invariant: never show a component as operational unless the probe/sample says so; uptime % must be computed from real HealthSample rows, not faked. If there's no history yet, say "collecting data", don't fabricate 100%.
- Tests must bite: use `stripCommentsAndStrings`/`stripComments` from `test/_source-tools.ts` for source tripwires; unit-test the incident auto-open/close state machine and uptime math with injected clock/samples (pure functions — factor them out so they're testable without a DB).
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean for your files; tests run via `npm test` (node:test).
- Do NOT run prisma db push/migrate, next build in place, git commit, deploy, or systemctl.

## Deliver
Typechecking code + tests. Final report: (1) exact worker/index.ts monitor-loop call line to add; (2) any new env vars; (3) what's real vs simulated; (4) test count; (5) confirmation the existing monitoring.ts exports still satisfy MarketingFooter + admin page. Report is data for me.

model ErrorLog {
  id          String   @id @default(cuid())
  level       String   @default("error") // error | warn | info

  userId      String?
  serverId    String?
  jobId       String?
  count       Int      @default(1)
  firstSeen   DateTime @default(now())
  lastSeen    DateTime @default(now())
  resolved    Boolean  @default(false)

  @@index([lastSeen])
  @@index([level, lastSeen])
  @@index([source])
}

/// Periodic health snapshots written by the worker monitor sweep — one row per
/// component per sweep. Powers uptime % and the health timeline (previously
/// every status render was an instantaneous probe with no history).
model HealthSample {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  component String // web | proxmox | worker | db
  status    String // operational | degraded | down
  latencyMs Int?
  detail    String?
  ts        DateTime @default(now())

  @@index([component, ts])
  @@index([ts])
}

/// An incident on the public status page — auto-opened when a component stays
/// unhealthy across sweeps, or posted by an operator. Gives the status page a
/// real incident history and per-incident timeline.
model StatusIncident {
  id         String    @id @default(cuid())
  component  String? // affected component, or null for platform-wide
  severity   String    @default("degraded") // degraded | down | maintenance
  title      String
  body       String    @default("")
  startedAt  DateTime  @default(now())
  resolvedAt DateTime?
  auto       Boolean   @default(false) // opened automatically vs by an operator
  createdAt  DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt  DateTime  @updatedAt

  @@index([startedAt])
  @@index([resolvedAt])
}

- Pure, DB-free functions (unit-tested with injected clock/samples): `uptimeFromSamples`, `bucketTimeline`, `decideIncident` (auto open/close), `worstStatus`, `autoIncidentCopy`.
